episodes.desc: Three gauges bullish, two neutral, one bearish -- SPY at $765.37, volatility calm at 9.6%, and CPI at 3.7% doing most of the work in a market arguing with itself.

episodes.title: The Dashboard Didn't Move. Central-Bank Week Will.
episodes.desc: All six gauges froze into central-bank week -- SPY at $759.97 between its two trend lines, CPI at 3.7%, and a market priced for one outcome until the Fed or the ECB changes its mind.

episodes.desc: Musk says 200+ neoclouds face 'guppy-level death' while CoreWeave and Nebius slide -- and Verizon's $2B AWS deal shows the demand side is fine; it's the suppliers being sorted.

episodes.title: Meta Just Answered the AI Funding Question -- With Your Shares
episodes.desc: Meta launched a $35B stock offering to fund its AI buildout, and the stock's round trip -- down on dilution, up on the plan -- answers the only question that matters now: not how much gets spent, but who pays for it.

episodes.title: The Dashboard Didn't Move. Central-Bank Week Will.
episodes.desc: All six gauges held exactly where Sunday left them: SPY $759.97, momentum +2.8%, volatility 9.5%, CPI 3.7%. A frozen dashboard is not a calm market -- it is a market waiting, and the Fed and the ECB both meet this week.

episodes.desc: France boards up its luxury stores while Swiss stocks outperform -- two rotations, one destination: somewhere quieter to stand.

episodes.title: 3.7% and Creeping: The Inflation Chart in One Look
episodes.desc: CPI has drifted from 2.9% to 3.7% in twelve months without a single spike -- the chart that argues against the Fed's settling thesis.

episodes.title: The $5 Cushion Holding Up a Bullish Dashboard

episodes.desc: CPI has drifted from 2.9% to 3.7% in thirteen months, in a straight line. The level isn't the story -- the direction is, and the October print decides it.

episodes.title: A Special Committee Is Not a Merger
